FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- THIS ONE IS NOT A RE-PIN, AND I DO NOT THINK IT IS A BUG IN YOUR CODE EITHER. 938adae2ef33, rc=11 at gate after 1173 s. Your three calibration re-pins all passed; this is the only failure.

    windows/scene/src/lib.rs:1994
    tests::flagship_appears_exactly_once
    "flagship duplicated as a settlement at its own coordinates"
      left: 2   right: 1

WHAT THE TEST ACTUALLY ASSERTS, from its own comment: that the flagship is not
EMITTED TWICE, once under each `kind`. It detects that by counting features
sharing the flagship's coordinates, on the reasoning that "two emissions of one
place necessarily share its coordinates."

That implication is true. ITS CONVERSE IS NOT, and the converse is what the
assertion actually tests. Two DISTINCT places sharing coordinates produce the
same count of 2 with nothing duplicated.

WHY YOUR CAMPAIGN IS THE ONE THAT BREAKS IT. Verified:

    pub struct ...Feature { name, kind, latitude, longitude }

There is no depth. A surface settlement and an underworld settlement at the
same latitude and longitude are, in this struct, the same point. Your campaign
adds peoples below ground; as soon as one of them sits under the flagship's
cell, the count reads 2 and the test fails without anything being emitted
twice.

WHAT I VERIFIED vs INFERRED, because you should not chase the wrong thing: the
missing depth field is verified from the struct. That an underworld settlement
specifically now occupies the flagship's coordinates is my inference from your
campaign's subject — I have not run the scene and enumerated the two features.
Do that first; it is one `tiles_scene` call and it names both features, and if
the second one is NOT an underworld settlement then my whole reading is wrong
and you have a real duplication bug.

THE HISTORY IS THE INTERESTING PART, AND IT IS WHY I WOULD NOT JUST PATCH THE
TEST. It already moved once for exactly this shape. Its comment says: "Keying
on name made this pass only while the flagship's own name happened to be
unique" — nine seed-42 settlements are called "Ka". So it went name -> position.
Position is now breaking for the same structural reason: the scene has no
identity, only descriptions, and each description becomes ambiguous as soon as
the world gains a way for two things to coincide. Names collided when names
stopped being identifiers; coordinates collide when the world stops being a
surface.

SO THE CHOICES ARE, roughly in ascending order of ambition:

  1. Assert on identity rather than any proxy — if a feature can name the
     settlement it came from, count emissions of THAT, and the test stops
     depending on what the world happens to make unique.
  2. Give Feature a depth (or a band discriminator). Decision 0356 retired the
     external clients, so scene schemas are no longer cross-repo contracts and
     this is changeable outright — but it is a schema change and belongs to
     whoever owns windows/scene, not to a census delivery.
  3. Narrow the test to the surface band. Cheapest, and it quietly gives up on
     the underworld ever being checked.

I would not pick for you and (2) in particular is not yours to decide inside
this candidate. If you want the fastest honest path, (1) or (3) with a comment
recording WHY — the third time this proxy breaks, whoever hits it should find
the first two written down.

Your other three pins are correct and landed in this run: homophony means
re-pinned with the witness/claim distinction spelled out, syllables, and the
four-site D5 restatement. That work is done and does not need revisiting.
